items.title: Charles Davis interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 23, 1997
items.q: I worked with Clark Terry... I was with his big band for a few years... I remember playing with Clark Terry’s band in Italy

ctx.x: What was your — did you have much big band experience over the years? With Sun Ra of course, but ...
I worked with Clark Terry, Thad Jones, the latest being Clifford Jordan. I was with his big band for a few years, playing the baritone, along with playing the tenor and alto in that band.
The baritone — your name comes up with baritone a lot.

items.title: Terry Clark — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: In the big band, Ernie Wilkins, who wrote for us. He played tenor [saxophone]. We had Charles Davis on baritone [saxophone].

ctx.x: The Big B-A-D Band. Oh, I didn’t write anything for the Big B-A-D Band. I’m talking about the combo, I wrote. No, I wasn’t too much into big-band writing. In the big band, Ernie Wilkins, who wrote for us. He played tenor [saxophone]. We had Charles Davis on baritone [saxophone]. We had Charlie Williams on alto [saxophone], Chris Woods.
